We have had long and valuable service from Arthur Penny and George Chantler our Honorary Starters but both of these gentlemen are adamant that it is time someone else took over.

The Committee proposed George Chantler and Jim Heathfield as Vice-Presidents and from the floor our 1972 Olympic trio of Cliff Brooks, Wilf Wesch and John Bicourt together with Bill Merryman were also put forward.
He finished 43rd of the 65 starters in 4hrs 34mins 52secs. It is good to see GEORGE CHANTLER about again. Last winter he had a serious illness and more recently his wife was ill.
Wally Wortley, 10th, led the Bels home with Mac 16th, George Chantler 17th and Arthur Whitehead 21st. Mac's training was a five times a week affair.

Our Marathon champion, Macdonald, despite a bad spell at about forty miles when he was nearly caught by George Chantler, finished very strongly, and George running his usual steady race also did very well indeed to finish inside seven hours.

George Chantler: We regret to inform our older members of the passing of a longtime friend and member.- George was a very active team member in his younger days and would have been a valuable member of our management team.
